sentences.text: Rule seven also covers radar, so here’s a scenario.
Imagine you’re heading out of Port Everglades on a rare foggy morning.
You glance at the radar and see a target about three miles ahead.
One look tells you almost nothing: where it’s going, how fast, whether it’ll pass clear.
Rule seven says radar must be used properly, with long-range scanning for early warning, and radar plotting or equivalent systematic observation.
Mark the target, watch it for a few minutes, and see how it moves.
And the rule adds a sentence worth memorizing: assumptions shall not be made on the basis of scanty information, especially scanty radar information.
